title: appointments._book_from_request
description: The payload of `whatsapp_inbox.request.approved`, VERBATIM (appointments#38). A manifest listener has no mapping layer — the relay hands the event payload straight to the command — so this schema describes what the emitting command accepted, not a shape of its own, and `additionalProperties` stays TRUE because the runtime stamps every event payload with its system params (`hub_id`, `now`, `new_id`, the business identity…). Anything stricter dead-letters every approval instead of booking it. Only `request_id` is required: an approval that bound nothing IS a valid event — this handler answers it with `appointments.booking_request.failed` so the inbox can say what is missing, which is the whole point of the issue. The four booking fields sit FLAT at the top level because `reads.params` can only address `payload.<field>`, which is what makes the authoritative catalogue lookups possible at all.

request_id.description: The request being materialised. It is the correlation of the hand-over: every answer this handler emits carries it back so the asking module can find its row.

customer_id.description: The customer, as a LINK to the `customers` module. Resolved authoritatively through `customers.get`; the snapshot on the appointment is frozen from that row, never from the message.

service_id.description: The service, as a link to the `services` catalogue. Name, price and duration come from the catalogue row.

staff_id.description: The professional, as a link to `staff`. Checked for being active, bookable and eligible for the service.

start_datetime.description: When it starts, ISO-8601. Re-validated against lead time, blocked agenda and overlap at THIS moment, not at the moment the message arrived.

duration_minutes.description: Optional override. Absent = the professional's override, else the catalogue duration, else the module default.

notes.description: What the customer asked for, in their own words, carried onto the appointment.
